title: Partner co-sell pipeline review - Silverline Partners
summary: Partner co-sell pipeline review covering joint targets, potential logo plays, technical gating (VPC/private deploys), commercial commit timelines, and next steps to enable joint outreach. Agreed to share co-sell deck, run list of top 3 target accounts, and schedule a technical deep-dive next week.
next_steps: Sofia to send co-sell deck, pricing sheet, and partner enablement one-pager by 2026-09-22
Silverline to share top 3 target accounts and procurement timelines by 2026-09-24
Schedule SE technical deep-dive with Derek for week of 2026-09-27
Marcus to prepare a short benchmark plan (latency/cost) for the two highest-priority accounts
action_items: Sofia Patel | Send co-sell deck & pricing sheet | 2026-09-22
Maya Rivera | Share top 3 accounts & procurement windows | 2026-09-24
Marcus Lin | Draft benchmark plan and checklist | 2026-09-25
Derek Wu | Provide architecture constraints and current infra notes (VPC, MTLs) | 2026-09-24
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we got about an hour. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Ethan (Silverline): Ethan here — Head of Alliances at Silverline.
[00:11] Maya (Silverline): Maya here, partner sales.
[00:13] Derek (Silverline): Derek, solutions.
[00:15] Marcus (Redwood SE): Marcus Lin from Redwood, SE.
[00:18] Sofia: Awesome. Quick agenda: pipeline review, co-sell motion, any technical blockers, and agree next steps.
[00:27] Ethan: Sounds good. I'll kick off with the pipeline — we've got five joint prospects we want to prioritize, two are, like, mid-market SaaS customers and three enterprise interesting ones.
[00:36] Maya: To be clear, prioritization is based on procurement timing — we have one RFP that may go live in October.
[00:41] Marcus: Cool, can you name the two main ones? Even high level is fine.
[00:46] Ethan: Sure — "Orchid Retail" is the mid-market one, and "Northbridge Financials" is the big enterprise — Northbridge is the one with heavy compliance needs, like data residency, SOC2 type and, uh, needs a private deployment.
[00:58] Sofia: Okay, Northbridge will be the one that triggers the Private/VPC conversation. Marcus, on our side, what's the gating for Private?
[01:06] Marcus: So for Private we need an infra checklist — VPC peering or customer-managed VPC, firewall rules, KMS integration for key management, and an audit-log forwarding plan. Also we need to confirm the model variants — e.g., whether they require a quantized model for local GPU footprints.
[01:24] Derek: On Northbridge's side they want HSM-backed keys and everything SOC 2 type II, also SAML/SSO integration for RBAC.
[01:31] Sofia: That's fine — we have existing Private deployments with KMS/HSM integrations and SAML SSO. We'll share the security pack.
[01:37] Ethan: Do you have any reference docs for that?
[01:39] Sofia: Yes, I'll attach the security brief and our SOC2 summary. Link: redwood.com/security (note: link shortened here).
[01:45] Marcus: Also from an ops perspective, for latency-sensitive workloads we recommend our Dedicated pool — lower jitter and dedicated GPU capacity — unless Northbridge wants full Private on-prem, in which case we can talk hybrid.
[01:56] Maya: Cost is a concern — how do Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private compare?
[02:00] Marcus: Quick, uh, summary: Hosted is easiest and cheapest to start but can have multi-tenant variability. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and latency for a committed price. Private has the highest ops lift but is required for strict compliance/residency. We have tooling to size the committed capacity — Redwood Optimize recommendations include batching and prefix caching to lower per-token cost.
[02:21] Ethan: For our co-sell pitch we need a simple statement on unit economics — e.g., estimated monthly cost for a 100k token/day workload under Dedicated.
[02:29] Sofia: Marcus, can you capture that as an action?
[02:31] Marcus: Yep — I'll run a rough calc and include assumptions.
[02:33] [00:34] Sofia: Great. Another question from Silverline: do you support region-specific deployments for EU data residency?
[02:39] Marcus: Yes, we have region pinned Dedicated pools and Private in EU regions. For GDPR-sensitive customers we can ensure no cross-region replication of logs.
[02:47] Derek: On the networking side, are we doing direct connect or VPN for the Private option?
[02:51] Marcus: We support both. For low-latency real-time inference direct connect is preferred; for initial trials VPN is usually sufficient.
[02:58] Maya: Who typically owns the procurement conversation? Is it the partner or Redwood?
[03:02] Sofia: Usually it's collaborative — partner introduces, we provide pricing and contract, and the partner gets co-sell credit. We'll walk through the co-sell motion in the deck.
[03:11] Ethan: Speaking of the deck, can we make sure it includes the co-sell commission splits, and an intro to joint logos we can use?
[03:17] Sofia: Yes, standard partner materials include a co-sell guide. I'll send that.
[03:21] [00:40] Marcus: Quick technical note — for Northbridge we recommend a deterministic latency SLO, so we may need to reserve capacity (Dedicated) and set autoscale thresholds. Also mention KV-cache priming for large context reuse to lower tokens.
[03:35] Derek: Priming and KV cache — will that require any changes to the customer app?
[03:39] Marcus: Minimal — we provide client libs and hooks. For heavy reuse you might want to store prompt prefixes in the cache layer; we can share example code.
[03:46] Ethan: For the RFP timeline, they want a security questionnaire filled out. Is that the "security pack" you mentioned?
[03:51] Sofia: Yes — SOC2 attestation, data flow diagrams, KMS/HSM description, and SAML integration notes. I'll attach the pack in the follow-up.
[03:59] Maya: Nice. For the mid-market prospect, Orchid Retail, they are probably fine with hosted but would like a POC for 30 days.
[04:06] Marcus: We can do a hosted POC; recommend using our sandbox API keys and pre-batched tests. We'll advise on the prompt sets for quality monitoring.
[04:14] Ethan: Are there any known limitations on model size for hosted POC?
[04:18] Marcus: Hosted supports up to the larger open models, but if they need a quantized 8-bit large model for lower cost we may recommend Dedicated or Private depending on GPU. We'll include model suggestions in the POC plan.
[04:29] Sofia: OK let's map owners: co-sell deck and pricing — Sofia. Benchmark plan and technical deep-dive — Marcus. Silverline to share top accounts and timelines — Maya/Ethan.
[04:39] Derek: On a deeper topic — Northbridge asks about audit log retention in Private vs Dedicated.
[04:44] Marcus: Private gives you full control over log retention; Dedicated we can increase retention as an add-on but logs may still be in Redwood managed storage depending on contract.
[04:54] Ethan: We should note that for Northbridge they'll likely ask for a runbook for incident response and SLAs.
[04:59] Sofia: Yep, we'll include a sample runbook and SLA terms.
[05:03] [00:50] Marcus: One more thing — competitors. Silverline mentioned PlatformX is active in two of these accounts, and Anthropic is on the radar for another. Tactically, we should call out where Redwood's lower total cost of ownership and dedicated latency performance differ.
[05:18] Maya: Can we get a short one-pager comparing Redwood to those competitors for partner enablement?
[05:22] Sofia: Yes, we'll add a competitive one-pager.
[05:25] Derek: For the technical deep-dive, I'd like a short benchmark plan: sample prompts, expected latency targets, and SLOs.
[05:31] Marcus: I'll draft that and include a simple A/B benchmark with and without KV cache and with batching.
[05:37] Sofia: Great. Any other blockers we haven't covered?
[05:40] Ethan: Not from our side. Just to confirm—what's the ideal timing for the RFP response for Northbridge?
[05:45] Maya: It's late Oct submission, so we need final pricing by early Oct.
[05:49] Sofia: We'll aim to get a proposal drafted by end of September so you have time to include it.
[05:55] Ethan: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[05:57] Sofia: Ok recap: Sofia will send the security pack, co-sell deck, and pricing; Marcus will send benchmark plan; Silverline will share targets and timelines; schedule SE deep-dive week of 9/27.
[06:10] [END]
